LESSON: SKIMMING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Reading 2.2 Speed Reading (2 Lessons) By the end of the sub- strand, the learner
Topic 2.3: Skimming for information

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Skimming for information. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: what they eat, etc) and accomplish given tasks. Why is it important to know the meaning of words being read?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the main information in given texts for comprehension
2. read texts fluently for communication
3. appreciate the role of fluency in reading comprehension

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SKIMMING FOR INFORMATION
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Skimming for information helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school and at home in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: SKIMMING FOR INFORMATION
Study Skimming for information like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify the main information in given texts for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the main information in given texts for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the main information in given texts for comprehension.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain “Skimming for information” in your own words using one local example.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the main information in given texts for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Read texts fluently for communication

What this means
In this part you learn to read texts fluently for communication. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read texts fluently for communication.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Show one correct way to practise Skimming for information.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read texts fluently for communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of fluency in reading comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of fluency in reading comprehension. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of fluency in reading comprehension.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of fluency in reading comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Skimming for information is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Explain “Skimming for information” in your own words using one local example. (skill: identify the main information in given texts for comprehension)

Example 2: Show one correct way to practise Skimming for information. (skill: read texts fluently for communication)

Example 3: Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of fluency in reading comprehension)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Skimming for information to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the main information in given texts for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: read texts fluently for communication.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of fluency in reading comprehension.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Skimming for information from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Skimming for information: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Skimming for information?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. what they eat, etc) and accomplish given tasks. Why is it important to know the meaning of words being read?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Skimming for information means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the main information in given texts for comprehension.
5. Be able to: read texts fluently for communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
